record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and the first 400 file paths only; code and paper contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports findings that qualify a general account of refusal representations by model family, including a single-direction finding for OLMo-3. It does not report the original ablation or addition tests.
record.gate_note: The README summarizes research findings about refusal routing. The listed ablation and steering tools, paper scripts, and result files do not by themselves establish that any intervention was run. No harmful-request compliance rates, harmless-request refusals, or general-capability outcomes are reported in the README.
record.test_reason: This is a software repository README. Its refusal statements are one-sentence summaries of a separate paper, [FL] arXiv:2609.14759. The README reports no method, no refusal or compliance rates, no ablation or addition outcomes, and no numbers beyond 'about three-quarters'. The visible text gives no basis for judging any version. The underlying FL paper should be read as its own study.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, with one correction. The README says moral knowledge forms in pretraining and refusal is a post-training construction reading only a slice of it. On OLMo-3 refusal levels off at a single harm direction, with about three-quarters of its causal input outside the moral subspace. Llama, GPT-OSS and Qwen differ. These are summaries of the FL paper, not results shown in the README.
record.recipe_differences: Tool and research-summary repository, not a reproduction of the original difference-in-means refusal ablation and addition recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports model-family differences and says the Qwen result is unresolved at the paper's sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Per the FL summary, on OLMo-3 the refusal gate reads a single harm direction, with about three-quarters of its causal input outside a moral subspace. Refusal reads different content across families: broad moral content in Llama, harm in GPT-OSS, unresolved in Qwen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: What content the refusal mechanism reads from (harm vs. broad moral content) differs across model families. This may bear on V5 once the FL paper's actual results are extracted.

record.problems: The README gives only a brief qualitative summary for the refusal findings; it omits the measurement procedure, prompt sets, numerical estimates beyond about three-quarters, and uncertainty details.
record.rows_left_out: No additional README refusal results were reported. The listed code, paper files, and output files were not read or run, so their contents are not extracted.

missing.what: Full results of the FL paper on harm-keyed refusal routing across model families (methods, interventions, numbers). Only README one-liners are available here.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T5 and its V4 limits_scope label are not supported. Nothing in the README measures refusal behaviour or direction count, so no verdicts are given. The FL paper should be searched and read separately.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-minus-harmless direction ablation or addition, refusal-rate outcome, or general-capability test is reported.
No weight-edit ablation or released-model refusal outcome is reported.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The README does not report affine or cone fits, or a direct test of whether other directions contribute to refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
Model-family summaries are given, but no transfer test of the same direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models is reported.
The README says post-training shapes refusal, but reports no comparison of training procedures or timing testing whether these determine a removable direction.
